recipes.name: Easy Turkey Chili
ingredients_raw: 1 (15.5 ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained
1 (15.5 ounce) can kidney beans, rinsed and drained
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add turkey; cook and stir until browned and crumbly, 5 to 7 minutes. Drain and discard any excess grease.

Add onion to the pot; cook and stir until translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in tomatoes, broth, all beans, chili powder, garlic, paprika, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper; bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with Cheddar cheese.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Turkey Chili
raw_recipe.description: Hearty turkey chili made with refried, kidney, and black beans.

review.reviewBody: Quick and easy. I really enjoyed this. Who thought you could make a pot of chili after getting home from work. For those of you who like your chili hot and spicy -- you will need to add something. This is great for the whole family.

I've never left a recipe review before because I'm what you would call "culinary challenged". But, I tried this and it was a total success! Super easy and super delicious! It irritates me when people post about how great a recipe is, but then make a bunch a changes to it. The only things I did differently were: I added an entire chopped onion, not just a half. And I added a 1/2 tsp of Cayenne - because my husband likes a little kick. And I added 2 cans of red beans and omitted the black because I don't care for black beans. This is definitely a meal you could make quickly after work or throw it a crockpot and let it cook all day on low.

I just made this tonight and turned out great! I used Rotel (canned tomatoes with chilies) instead of regular diced canned tomatoes to give it a little more spice. Also, I did this in a crockpot instead of stovetop. I sauteed the garlic, onions and ground turkey (salt, pepper and garlic powder on the turkey before cooking to season it). I put the rest of the ingredients in the crockpot first and mixed together. after the turkey is cooked, I added the mixture to the crockpot, mixed and cooked on high for 4 hours (or low for 8 hours). I also I left out the Kidney beans (because I do not like them)... and it turned out fine without them. I also added a can of corn to give it a little color. Great recipe! My son ate 3 bowls!!

I love this recipe! I changed it up a bit. Here is what I did for 6 servings... I used (Lite Life Smart Ground 12 ounces) Veggie Meat Substitute instead of turkey. I added 6 peeled and diced carrots. I used kidney beans instead of black beans. I used 1 tbsp chili powder instead of 2 1/2 tbsp. Instead of crushed tomatoes, puree in food processor-1 can 14 oz. Glen Muir Organic diced tomatoes and 2 dried/soaked/seeded pasilla peppers.

Good base. I sauteed onions, salt and 1 green pepper in the oil for 5 min before adding the turkey and a bit more salt. Added garlic once turkey was cooked. Added beans tomatoes, spices as well as 1 celery stock cut in half, can of corn and can of diced tomatoes with green chilies. Increased stock to 3 cups. Once mixture was boiling, added 1/3 cup of quinoa for an extra hint of flavor and texture. Let this simmer for a good 30 to 40 min.

I have many wonderful chili recipes and this is my husband’s favorite. He generally prefers ground beef. I mostly followed the recipe. I have to watch my salt and as the tomatoes and refried beans already contain salt, I figured it didn’t need much. I used reduced sodium chicken broth and no- salt kidney and black beans. I didn’t add any additional salt and only had two tbsp of chili powder. The rest of the spices , I used as stated in the recipe. I also added 1/4 tsp black pepper. It was delicious and we didn’t miss the extra salt! Thank you!

Made it with ground beef since I didn't have ground turkey. My kids like the black beans much more than kidney beans and the refried beans as a thickener is brilliant. Kids didn't even know it was there just said it was delicious. Spice level is nice. Will definitely make again.
(11/21/18) I've made it several times now with the turkey. I omit the kidney beans since the kids don't like the texture. This chili is too liquid at first. It needs to simmer uncovered more than the 30 minutes until it's the right consistency (according to my husband). The flavors are wonderful.

This was easy and delicious! I upped the amount of spices for more kick. Also, I let it cook all day in the crock pot, but would definitely do it again as a quick meal! When it was time to eat we topped it with our usual cheese, tortilla chips, and sour cream!

This is really tasty! I cut the recipe in half and only used a can of kidney beans. I didn't have chili powder, but had cayenne and a smoked chipotle powder. Leftovers were even better with the flavors blending over night. I'll definitely make it again!

Easy and awesome! I used northern white beans rather than black beans, rotel tomatoes as others have suggested. Rather than canned broth I dissolved better than bouillon in hot water prior to adding it to the pot. I also used one pound of ground beef and one pound of turkey since I was doubling the recipe and that's what I had on hand. The chili was amazing!!!

You are a genius. The refries makes this recipe magical! Instead of black beans, I used 50% less sodium chili beans. I also added liquid smoke. Also added some hoisin sauce to neutralize the acidity of the crushed tomatoes. Really yummy.

I followed the recipe exactly. I found it lacked flavor and depth, and didn’t have much tomato flavor. I think the chicken broth watered down the flavor. I added smoked paprika and a small can of Rotel, which improved the flavor. Its still lacking something. I appreciate that I didn’t have to go grocery shopping as i had all ingredients at home. Next time I will make my standard chili.

I made this recipe as written (but garnished with cheddar jack). As written, this is a good base recipe with potential. It is a no-frills chili that would be good for those who do not like spicy things. It is also a bit on the watery side. My family wasn't the biggest fans, but we could see how some may like it.
This was super tasty. Due to the spiciness, I skip the chili powder when making for the kids and it is still really good! Add some sour cream for a nice added flavor :) thanks for sharing!
it needs a little more heat.
Super, ridiculously easy. I’m someone who makes chili but won’t eat it until the next day so it develops the best flavor, but this was perfect the day I made it and the next couple days as leftovers!

I just make this and it is great and relatively quick and you can spice it up if you want, but I would taste it about half way through to see if you have to add something to give it more kick. But it was fine the way it was for me,will be making it again.
Pretty good but needed more seasoning. Added some chipotle seasoning.
